title: The Quran: Surah 2, al-Baqarah (The Heifer), verse 286
author: Tradução inglesa de Talal Itani (ClearQuran)
tradition: Texto sagrado do Islão, século VII
intro: Lição sobre a Surata 2, versículo 286. O texto inglês é a tradução de Talal Itani, reproduzida sem alterações; as notas de língua, perguntas, discussão e escrita são material pedagógico separado, baseado apenas no que o próprio texto diz.

source.title: Quran English Translation: Clear, Pure, Easy to Read Modern English
source.edition: Edition A (uses the word 'Allah' to refer to the Creator)

questions.q: According to the verse, what does Allah not do?
options: Burden any soul beyond its capacity
questions.why: O versículo começa com 'Allah does not burden any soul beyond its capacity.'

options: the amount someone can bear or do
questions.why: 'Capacity' é a capacidade, o que alguém consegue suportar.

questions.q: The prayer says 'do not burden us with more than we have strength to bear'. How does this connect to the first sentence?
options: It asks for the same thing the first sentence states
questions.why: A primeira frase diz 'beyond its capacity' e a oração pede 'not... more than we have strength to bear'.

questions.q: How many times does the prayer start a sentence with 'Our Lord,'?
questions.why: A oração tem três frases a começar com 'Our Lord, do not...'.

questions.q: Which sentence best sums up the verse?
options: It tells a story about a king
It lists the names of places
It says no soul is burdened beyond its capacity, and gives a prayer asking for ease, forgiveness and help
questions.why: A primeira parte afirma e a segunda é uma oração.

B2.discussion: The verse says no soul is burdened beyond its capacity. How can this idea help someone who is having a difficult time?
B2.writing: Write 80 to 100 words: Explain in your own words what the verse says and what the prayer asks for.

questions.q: What is 'to its credit' in the first part of the verse?
questions.why: O versículo diz: 'To its credit is what it earns'.

questions.q: 'Pardon' in 'and pardon us' is closest to:
What do the words 'if we forget or make a mistake' show about the speakers?
options: That they ask for help with ordinary human limits
questions.why: A oração admite 'forget' e 'make a mistake'.

questions.q: The prayer repeats 'Our Lord, do not...' three times. What does the repetition do?
options: It builds a pattern of three requests, each about blame or a burden
questions.why: As três frases pedem para não ser condenado e para não ser sobrecarregado.

options: The verse moves from a prayer to a story
The verse is a list of laws
The verse moves from a statement about limits to a prayer for ease, forgiveness and help
questions.why: A afirmação inicial é seguida de uma oração entre aspas.

C1.discussion: The verse first states a principle and then turns it into a prayer. How does the prayer change the way the principle sounds?
C1.writing: Write 120 to 150 words: Explain how the repetition of 'Our Lord' shapes the second half of the verse.

questions.q: How does the verse describe what a soul earns and what it commits?
options: What it earns is lost, and what it commits is kept
To its credit is what it earns, and against it is what it commits
What it earns is hidden, and what it commits is praised
What it earns is shared, and what it commits is forgotten
questions.why: O versículo diz 'To its credit is what it earns, and against it is what it commits'.

questions.q: 'To its credit' and 'against it' work as:
options: two names of the same thing
opposites that mark gain and loss
questions.why: 'To its credit' é a favor e 'against it' é contra.

questions.q: The prayer is placed in quotation marks after a statement. What does that change?
options: It makes the verse a story
It turns a statement about Allah into words the speakers address to Him
It changes the topic to a place
It makes the verse a list
questions.why: As aspas marcam a oração dirigida a 'You'.

questions.q: The prayer has three sentences beginning 'Our Lord, do not...' and a closing sentence beginning 'You are'. What is the effect?
options: The sentences change the topic each time
The three requests build a pattern, and the closing sentence gives the reason for asking
The closing sentence ends the prayer without a reason
questions.why: A última frase, 'You are our Lord and Master', fecha o padrão e justifica o pedido.

questions.q: Which description of the verse is best supported?
options: A statement of a limit, a balanced pair of earning and committing, and a prayer built on repetition
questions.why: Cada parte do versículo tem uma função distinta.

C2.discussion: The verse is built from a balanced pair ('to its credit... against it') and a prayer built on repetition. What does each device add?
C2.writing: Write 150 to 200 words: Analyse how the verse is built, referring to specific words and to the pattern of repetition.
